title: Prototype pollution and ReDoS in SheetJS xlsx on file read
shortFix: Back-ports SheetJS's fixes for CVE-2023-30533 (prototype pollution) and CVE-2024-22363 (ReDoS) onto the frozen npm 0.18.5 baseline.
longFix: npm's `xlsx@0.18.5` is the last version SheetJS published to the registry; later fixed releases ship only via cdn.sheetjs.com. This fork ports two upstream fixes: a guard in `sheet_insert_comments` rejecting comment refs that decode to negative coordinates (CVE-2023-30533, from 0.19.3), and an indexOf-based core-property scanner replacing a backtracking regex (CVE-2024-22363, from 0.20.2).
summary: Two vulnerabilities are reachable when `XLSX.read()` parses an attacker-supplied spreadsheet. CVE-2023-30533: a crafted (threaded) comment whose cell `ref` is `__proto__` causes `sheet[ref]` to resolve to `Object.prototype`, which is then mutated — polluting every object in the process. CVE-2024-22363: a crafted `docProps/core.xml` with many unclosed property tags triggers catastrophic backtracking in the core-property regex (a ~2 MB file takes ~50 seconds to parse, a denial of service).
fixExplanation: Prototype pollution: `sheet_insert_comments` now returns early when `decode_cell(comment.ref)` yields negative row/column, so a non-address ref such as `__proto__` can never reach `sheet[comment.ref]`. ReDoS: `parse_core_props` now locates each property tag with `String#indexOf` (`str_match_xml`) instead of a `([\s\S]*?)` regex that re-scanned from every opening tag. Both are direct ports of SheetJS's own fixes; a cross-version equivalence test confirms legitimate files parse identically to upstream 0.18.5.
